newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Report on SAfrican oil deals probe out soon-Maduna.
newsitem.headline: Report on SAfrican oil deals probe out soon-Maduna.

text.p: South African Mineral and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna said on Wednesday he had bypassed the auditor-general's office to get an independent assessment of losses to the state from illegal oil deals.

Maduna told parliament in answer to questions on a probe of alleged irregularities in the state-owned Strategic Fuel Fund (SFF) that the investigation had found that 173 million rand had not been properly accounted for.
Auditor-General Henry Kluever's office had previously investigated SFF's books and had found nothing amiss.

"I will tell you without seeking to impugn the authority or the integrity of the office of the auditor-general, I felt constrained to go out of the ranks of the state and look for people who are independent who would be able to give me the answers that I was looking for," Maduna said.
"The report is coming pretty soon," he said, adding: "It will reveal more. It will embarrass some people.
"They will have to say exactly what was happening to our money.

"They will have to say that this is how, short of a big fire, they lost stock to the tune of 170 million rand. They will also have to say why they were paying 7.5 US cents to certain people in respect of Egyptian crude when those monies were not due and payable."
He did not give further details on the content of the report.
